V2-01 and V2-02 resolve my v1 comments. The distinction between lost/corrupt review materials (Cannot assess) and a faithfully captured short or truncated response (assess what is there, record the format problem, exclusion only under a separate prespecified rule) is the right one. Wrong-only components earning no credit and names-only earning nothing (X26, X39) matches the trial adjudication.

Per-domain conditional branches for Sub49 C06 remove the risk that one mention of speed triggers an inventory of cadence and symmetry. Agree that G03 applies to all five tasks regardless of whether the report calls its values comparisons.

V2-04 adopts my request: the Sub50 statement that in-range speed does not establish matching satisfies both its C01 component and the comparability half of G03, with the inference limitation still required. No second sentence is sought. Agree.

I proposed the numeric location tolerance as optional and do not require it. Retaining semantic, precision-based review with documented adjudication of disputed locations is acceptable. If formal rating shows repeated disagreement over "approximately", the convention can be added then with evidence.

V2-03 and V2-06 are acceptable: correct-then-contradicted receives coverage plus a logged E01, wrong-only receives no coverage, explicit retractions are read in context, ambiguous alternatives go to pending coverage adjudication rather than Cannot assess, and presuppositions in follow-up questions join the existing issue group. One non-blocking addition for the Future rating fields sheet: give the coverage record a "contradicted_elsewhere" flag (yes/no) and the "adjudication_status" field named in RUBRIC section 2, so the analysis plan can later separate "covered and uncontradicted" from "covered but contradicted" without re-rating. The rubric semantics need not change.

This is the written rule that was missing after the trial and I confirm it.

I confirm the distinction: reference-anchored descriptive magnitude is not a severity class. Suggested improvement, not blocking: the synthetic sentence currently contains its own justification ("moderate here describes that relative position, not a clinical severity class"), which real reports will not include. A more realistic calibration example is: "GPS-like 6.86 lies above the supplied median 5.1 and below the pooled 95th percentile 10.7, a moderate deviation from the reference." The proposed assessment (acceptable descriptive wording, no severity grade) should apply to that bare form as well; if the panel would not accept the bare form, the rule in section 7 needs narrowing.
